writeup: TIC 59464503 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 0.9939 days. TESS photometry reveals a primary eclipse causing 6.13% dimming, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The transit signal achieved a detection significance of 359.2 in the box-least-squares periodogram, and pixel-level analysis confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 37.2, though the centroid offset of 2.5 arcsec from the target's nominal position warrants note. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously unknown object. The machine-learning screening score of 0.60 indicates moderate confidence that this represents a genuine astrophysical source, and the data passed all quality checks without flags.
